why: 会 is for skills you learned: 我会游泳.

q: May I sit here? =
why: 可以 comes right after 我 and asks for permission.

q: Which is the pinyin of 想 (would like)?
why: 想 has the third tone: xiǎng.

q: I'd like to eat at home tonight =
why: When first, then 想, then where, and the verb last.

q: I don't want to go =
why: 不 goes in front of 想: 我不想去.

p: I'd like to drink a cup of tea
why: Tea in a cup takes the measure word 杯: 一杯茶.

p: I want to study at the library
why: Where it happens goes before the verb: 想在图书馆学习.

p: I can speak a little Chinese
why: 会 is for a skill you learned, like a language; 是 is not "can".
可以 gives permission: 你可以进来.
A skill you never learned takes 不会.

p: Waiter, I'd like a bowl of noodles.
why: With a thing and no verb, want is 要 (or 想要).

p: I'd like two cups of coffee
why: Coffee in a cup takes the measure word 杯, and two before it is 两.

p: I'd like to eat at home (use 想)
why: Where it happens goes before the verb: 想在家吃饭.
A skill takes 会, and its no is 不会, not 没.

q: I bought three tickets =
why: 了 goes right after the verb: 买了三张票.

q: Which is the pinyin of 买 (to buy)?
why: 买 has the third tone; mài (fourth tone) is 卖, to sell.

q: I was busy yesterday =
why: A state in the past takes no 了: 我昨天很忙.

q: I didn't go yesterday =
why: After 没 there is no 了.

q: It's gotten hot. =
why: 了 at the end shows a change: 热了.

p: I didn't go to work yesterday (begin with 我)
why: Time goes before the verb, and after 没 there is no 了.
Apples take the measure word 个: 三个苹果.
了 at the end shows a change, and 冷 needs no 是.
了 right after the verb shows the buying is done.
For something that did not happen, use 没, not 不.
了 at the end shows a change: 我饿了.
Tickets take the measure word 张, and two before it is 两.

p: I didn't go to the bank yesterday
why: Time goes before the verb, and after 没 there is no 了.
了 at the end shows a change, and adjectives take no 是.

q: I'm eating =
why: 在 before the verb means in the middle of; 是 is not "am".

q: Which is the pinyin of 在?
why: 在 has the fourth tone: it falls, zài.

q: What are you doing? =
why: The question word stays where the answer goes: 在做什么.

q: I'm going to Shanghai tomorrow (a plan) =
why: A plan takes no 在; 在 is for what is going on now.

q: He's at home watching TV =
why: Where it happens goes before the verb, and 呢 goes at the very end.

p: I'm watching TV at home right now
why: Where it happens goes before the verb, and 呢 goes at the end.

p: We're having class right now (use 正在)
why: 正在 goes before the verb: 我们正在上课.
Chinese has no -ing: 在 + verb, and 是 is not "are".
在 or 正在 before the verb shows the action is going on.
呢 at the end goes with 正在 for right now.

p: Mom is on the phone in the kitchen.
why: 在 + place says where it is happening: 在厨房.
Chinese has no -ing: 在 or 正在 goes before the verb.
Where it happens goes before the verb: 在图书馆学习.

p: What are you doing? (to a friend)
why: 什么 stays where the answer goes, after 在 + verb.

q: I'm going to the bank to change money =
why: Go to the place first, then what you do there: 去银行换钱.

q: Which is the pinyin of 去 (to go)?
why: 去 has the fourth tone: qù.

q: She rides her bike to school =
why: 骑 for a bike, and how you go comes before 去.

q: Which verb means "ride" for buses, the subway and planes?
why: 坐 (literally sit) is for anything you ride inside; 骑 is for bikes.

q: He's coming to my place for dinner =
why: 来 + place first, then what he will do: 来我家吃饭.

p: I'm going to the supermarket to buy things
why: Where you go comes before the verb of what you do there: 去超市买东西.

p: I go to school by subway
why: How you go comes before the verb 去: 坐地铁去学校.

p: Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to see the Great Wall (begin with 我)
why: Time goes before both verbs: 我明天去北京看长城.

p: I'm going to the supermarket to buy things.
why: 买 (mǎi) is buy; 卖 (mài) is sell.

p: I ride my bike to work.
why: You ride a bike astride: 骑自行车.

p: He's coming to my place for dinner.
why: 来 + place: he comes to my place, then eats.

p: I'm going to the bank to change money
why: Where you go comes before the verb of what you do there: 去银行换钱.

p: I take the subway to work
why: How you go comes before the verb: 坐地铁去上班.

p: I'm going to the store to buy two bottles of water
hint: 商店 (store) · 买 · 两 · 瓶 · 水
why: Water in a bottle takes the measure word 瓶, and two before it is 两.

q: Are you busy? =
why: No 很 and no 吗: just 忙不忙.

q: Which is the pinyin of 去不去？
why: In a verb-not-verb question 不 takes the neutral tone: qù bu qù.

q: Do you have a car? =
why: 有 is negated with 没, so the question is 有没有.

q: Do you like coffee? =
why: A two-character verb: 喜不喜欢 or 喜欢不喜欢, with no 吗.

q: How do you answer 你去不去？ with yes?
why: Answer with the verb itself: 去 or 不去.

p: Are you coming tomorrow? (begin with 你)
why: Time goes before the verb, even in a question: 你明天来不来？
Books take the measure word 本: 这本书贵不贵？

p: Do you have an older brother?
why: 有 takes 没, so the question is 有没有, with no 吗.
Verb + 不 + verb makes the question: 去不去.

p: Do you have a Chinese book?
why: 有 is negated only with 没: 有没有.
Say the whole verb again after 不: 喜欢不喜欢.

p: Are you coming tomorrow? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
why: Time goes before the verb: 你明天来不来？

p: Do you want this cup of tea? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
why: A cup of something takes the measure word 杯: 这杯茶.

p: Is your older brother a teacher? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
why: 是不是 already asks the question, so there is no 吗.

q: I'm a student too =
why: 也 goes after the subject and before the verb.

q: Which is the pinyin of 也 (also)?
why: 也 has the third tone: yě.

q: We're all American =
why: 都 comes after 我们 and before the verb.

q: I haven't eaten yet =
why: 还没 + verb means not yet, with no 了.

q: None of us is going =
why: 都不 means none; 不都 means not all.

p: My dad is a teacher too
why: 也 goes before the verb, never at the end like English too.

p: We all like to drink tea
why: 都 goes after 我们 and before the verb: 我们都喜欢喝茶.
都 goes before the verb 在: 他们都在家.
也 (also) goes before 是: 她也是美国人.
都 (all) looks back at 我们: 我们都是学生.
还没 means not yet.
也 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.
都 goes before the verb, and cats take the measure word 只.

p: My mom and dad are both busy
why: 都 goes before the verb or adjective, and adjectives take 很, not 是.

q: Let's go =
why: 吧 at the end of a 我们 sentence means let's.

q: Which is the pinyin of 请 (please)?
why: 请 has the third tone: qǐng; qíng with the second tone is 晴, sunny.

q: Don't worry =
why: 别 + verb means don't; 不 only says not.

q: Come in, please =
why: 请 goes first, then the verb.

q: Could you give me a hand? =
why: 麻烦你 goes first, then the request.

p: Let's eat at home (begin with 我们)
why: Where it happens goes before the verb, and 吧 goes at the end.

p: Let's go to the hospital tomorrow (begin with 我们)
why: Time goes before the verb: 我们明天去医院吧.
请 goes first, then 别 + verb for don't: 请别担心.
吧 at the end makes it a suggestion: let's.
别 or 不要 + verb means don't.
请 goes before the verb: 请坐.

p: Let's go to the supermarket tomorrow
why: Time goes before the verb, and 吧 at the end makes it let's.

p: Let's buy two bottles of water
why: Water in a bottle takes the measure word 瓶, and two before it is 两.
别 or 不要 + verb means don't; 没 is for what didn't happen.

q: tea and coffee =
why: 和 joins two nouns: 茶和咖啡.

q: Which is the pinyin of 和 (and)?
why: 和 has the second tone: hé; hē with the first tone is 喝, to drink.

q: Would you like noodles or rice? =
why: In a question, or is 还是, and it needs no 吗.

q: I'm tired and I want to sleep =
why: 和 joins nouns, not sentences: just pause.

q: I'll go on Saturday or Sunday =
why: In a statement, or is 或者.

p: Wang Ming and I are going together (begin with 我)
why: 一起 goes before the verb: 我和王明一起去.

p: I'll go on Saturday or Sunday (begin with 我)
why: Time goes before the verb, and in a statement or is 或者.

p: Do you want this one or that one?
why: In a question that asks someone to choose, or is 还是; 和 is and.

p: Would you like tea or coffee?
why: In a question, or is 还是.

p: My mom and I are going together.
why: 和 joins two people: 我和我妈妈.

p: I'll go on Saturday or Sunday.
why: In a statement, or is 或者.

p: My mom and I are going to the supermarket together
why: 一起 goes before the verb: 一起去超市.

p: Would you like tea or coffee? (to a customer)
why: In a question, or is 还是.

p: I'd like a bowl of noodles and a cup of tea (use 要)
why: Noodles in a bowl take the measure word 碗, and tea in a cup takes 杯.
